newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma eases petrol rationing to stop price rise.
newsitem.headline: Burma eases petrol rationing to stop price rise.

text.p: Burma's military government on Friday eased its tight petrol rationing policy in a bid to control rising black market prices, a government official said on Friday.
Those with coupon books could fill up their tanks with petrol or diesel twice a week at nine of Rangoon's 41 government-owned filling stations, he said.

The petrol must be bought in a combination of U.S.-dollar denominated foreign exchange certificates (FECs) and kyats at a much higher rate than is charged for the regular weekly quota of two to four gallons of petrol per week.
"This measure is intended to help those who really need fuel for their own consumption," a high-ranking official from Myanma Petroleum Product Enterprise told Reuters.

"Everyone who has the fuel purchase book issued by our department can buy as much fuel as his tank can hold," he said, adding that the measure was designed to prevent people making a profit from selling surplus fuel.
Analysts said the new rule should help stabilise fuel prices which have been rising recently on the black market despite efforts by the military government to keep them in check.
Rumours have spread that the government has been unable to find new suppliers of crude oil, residents said, but local analysts blamed the price rise on an increase in demand and strict rationing.

Supplies for the black market come from rations sold by civil servants seeking to boost meagre wages, industry source said. Although selling fuel on the black market is illegal, the government has traditionally turned a blind eye.

Petrol in Rangoon was selling for about 300-320 kyats per gallon on the black market on Friday. The government sells its weekly rations at 25 kyats per gallon and the new measures announced on Friday charge 1.40 FECs plus 10.55 kyats per gallon of petrol.
One dollar bought about 169 kyats on the black market on Friday, and the official rate was about six kyats to the dollar.
